cells.date: Śaka 1105, Śōbhakṛit, Āśvayuja, amāvāsyā, Monday, Vyatīpāta.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village called Kuḷkuṇṇuru to 1,000 learned Brāhmaṇas who belonged to various gōtras. Published in Indian Antiquary Vol. IV, pp. 274ff; but no plates are here.

cells.location: Tiruvā-ppāḍi (hamlet of Poṇṇēri)
cells.place: On a stone set up near the dhvajastambha in the Kari-Krishṇa-Peru[mā]l temple.
cells.remarks: States that this is the chakra-stone set up to mark the village Āḷālu-Vairamaṅgalam which had been given as the śrōtriyam for the conduct of worship in the temple of Kari-Krishṇa-Perumāḷ at Tiruvā-ppāḍi. cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Characters belong to the 10th century A.D. Seems to register a gift of land made for offerings to the temple of Chiṅtāmaṇīśvara at Chiṅtāmaṇi in Paṭṭaṇakkūṟṟam, a sub-division of the West Coast by Kuḍiṭaṅgi Paṭṭalakan, who stipulated that the tenants of this land should annually supply oil to the temple at the rate of 10 nāḻi for every half-site.

cells.place: On six stray stones found scattered in the compound of the same temple.
cells.remarks: The writing belongs to the 13th century, A.D. Records the names of donors who presented paving and other stones to the temple evidently during construction. One of these was Śīraḷadēvan alias Taninirunṛan-Paḷḷavaraiyar, a lady of the royal family of the village, who made such a gift for the maṇḍapa of Kūttāḍumdēva (Naṭarāja). The other donors were (1) Nambi-Āḷvān, son of Tiruvarasu-iḷai-nīr-uṇṇān, (2) Peṇṇagaḍa-uḍaiyān Pichchan, (3) Śiya-pādan, (4) a resident of the village, (5) Tiruvāḍi-uḍaiyār and (5) Udaiyār, son of Kiḍārattaraiyar.

cells.location: Kurijil

cells.remarks: Registers the grant of land as kaṭṭugaṭṭage at the village Guṇḍalhalli alias Nārasāpura to the Hīḍe the rate of produce to be paid by the tenant. The gift was made by Dōvapa, son of Koṇḍapa Timmaṇa, the sthānīka of the Nārasādeva temple to a certain Nārasādeva, son of Alapa for digging a tank in which belonged to the temple and the land in the village of Guṇḍalhalli including the surrounding lands under cultivation. A portion of the land was also given to the same person as daśabandham under certain stipulations.

A plot of land was endowed to him under the tank at Būdali. His grandson Māḍa-Mutta-rasa, son of Kēta-Muttarasa, endowed this kaṇāḍu. Fragmentary. Refers to a certain Mōḍammaṇ as ruling the nāḍu and mentions three persons Gaṅga, Gāṅga-Rapaṅga and Malla.

cells.place: On an eighth hero-stone set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: States that the king was ruling the nāḍu and Sāte-arasa of the Vaidumba-kula was administering this village, Kōpakki attacked the village after collecting (the army of) the three kōṭṭas and lifted the cattle, and that Pōrigāyattē, son of Sūrapārasa of the Vaidumba-kula, fought the army of the enemy and drove them out and secured victory to the king and to himself, but was killed in the fight. A plot of land was endowed in his memory.

cells.location: Gaḷagānāth
cells.place: On a slab set up in the temple of Gaḷagēśvara.
cells.date: Chāḷukya- Vikrama year, 5 (in words), Raudra, Jyēshṭha, amāvāsya, Sunday, saṅkrānti, solar eclipse. [date-calculation appendix, No. 42: Chajukya-Vikrama year 5 (in words), Raudra, Jyéshthu, amivasyé, Sunday, sank- ranti, solar eclipse. Probably = A.D. 1080, June 20. There was asolar eclipse on this day. The week-day was, however, Saturday and not Sunday as cited in the record. But the DakshinSyana-sankranti occurred on Wednesday, 24th June.]
cells.remarks: Records that the country was being governed by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vīra-Nolamba-Pallava Permāṇadi, the king's brother. Describes the conquests of the Chōḷa, Lāḷa and other kings achieved by Nolamba-Pallava. Records a gift of thirty gadyāṇas made by Mokari Bammayya, the subordinate of Vīra-Noḷamba for constructing a maṇḍapa in the temple of Gaḷagēśvara at Phaḷḷuni-tīrtha for the merit of his mother Jōgi- yabbe, when Trailōkyamalla Vīra-Noḷamba Pallava was governing Banavāse-Twelve-thousand, Sāntalige-1,000, etc.

The gift was made with the permission of the king. The record gives the spiritual descent of Arhanandi-Bējadēva who belonged to the Koṇḍakuṇḍa-anvaya, Mūḷa-saṅgha, Dēśī-gaṇa and Pustaka-gachchha.
